name: Ellora Caves & Kailasa Rock Temple
description: Cave 16 (Kailasa Temple) is the largest single monolithic rock excavation in the world, carved vertically downward from a solid basalt cliff.
history: Showcases 34 major monasteries and temples representing Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain traditions carved side by side in religious harmony.
construction: Over 200,000 tonnes of basalt rock were chiseled away from top to bottom by hand over generations without scaffolds.
architecture: Full-scale Dravidian temple standing two stories high, adorned with life-sized elephant statues, columned mandapas, and mythological bas-reliefs.
significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1983; an unparalleled feat of rock engineering.
currentStatus: Standing pristine in Aurangabad District, Maharashtra, India.
